chapter: Benny Meroff and Chicago's jazz scene
title: The Oriental Theater shows and the Smiling Skies record
summary: At the Oriental he fronts a jazz band-within-a-band with Lennie Cohen and Don Forney and records Smiling Skies in the theater basement, later mistaken for Bix.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: theaters - so, that changed everything. And, of course, as I said -- we were worried whether the Marks Brothers might dump us and put one of their own big bands in but they didn't because, as I said, we had the best theater stage band in all of Chicago. So, off we go to the Oriental-- and it was a fantastic theater, and it was such fun not to move around so much; of course, the shows were harder there. The shows were really bigger there; they had more dancing girls and more big celebrities - such as Jean Harlow and that caliber of stars, you know and, uh, although the one thing that we'd start to do now - get down there at this Oriental Theater, there was little Lennie Cohen on the clarinet and a guy named Don Forney on the trombone and myself made a front line for a jazz band; we had a jazz band within a band and we got a chance for a recording contract and that's when I made a thing called "Smiling Skies"; we made that in the basement of the theater. They brought all electric equipment down and that record, I guess, that's the first time I ever played something that sounded like Bix because some guys in a discography said - oh, look, we unearthed the new Bix record and, because I had to correct that and I hadn't heard it and when I did hear it, I couldn't believe it was me playing. You know, because I didn't realize I had picked up as much from Bix as I---

---did -- I guess this was one time I was really trying to sound like him in a way. But, anyway, they-- the downtown-- you know, we worked in the theater through '29 and '30--- yeah - '29 and '30 and, then, of course, the theater business got real bad. And, Meroff
